title: DecryptionKey::agree_ecdh default impl silently returns Err for all KARI recipients — ECDH decrypt silently fails
description:
## Problem

In `smime-tree/src/key.rs`, the `DecryptionKey` trait provides a default implementation of `agree_ecdh`:

```rust
fn agree_ecdh(
    &self,
    _ephemeral_pub: &[u8],
    _algorithm: &KariAlgorithm,
) -> Result<Vec<u8>, SmimeError> {
    Err(SmimeError::UnsupportedAlgorithm("ECDH agree_ecdh not implemented".into()))
}
```

This means any implementor of `DecryptionKey` who does not explicitly override `agree_ecdh` will silently fail to decrypt any message encrypted to them using KARI (EC key agreement / `KeyAgreeRecipientInfo`). The caller sees `SmimeError::UnsupportedAlgorithm` rather than a clear error indicating that ECDH was not implemented.

## What goes wrong

An EC key implementor who only reads the required trait methods (`decrypt_cek`, `matches_recipient`) will miss that ECDH requires `agree_ecdh`. Their `matches_recipient` will correctly identify them as the recipient, but `decrypt` will return an error as if the algorithm is not supported — indistinguishable from a genuine algorithm mismatch.

This is especially dangerous because:
1. There is no doc comment on the default impl warning that EC-key implementors MUST override it.
2. The method name `agree_ecdh` is not mentioned in the `DecryptionKey` trait doc — an EC key implementor reading the trait docs would see `decrypt_cek` and `matches_recipient` but not know `agree_ecdh` exists.
3. The error message says 'not implemented' but is surfaced as `UnsupportedAlgorithm`, the same error used for genuinely unsupported algorithms.

## Files

- `smime-tree/src/key.rs` — `DecryptionKey` trait definition
- `smime-tree/src/decrypt.rs` — `process_kari` calls `key.agree_ecdh`

## What goes wrong if left as-is

EC key implementors will write a `DecryptionKey` impl that appears to compile correctly, passes all type checks, but silently fails to decrypt any ECDH-encrypted message. The error they get provides no indication that they forgot to implement `agree_ecdh`.
